info.title: Notosaurus relay
info.description:
The Notosaurus relay's API, version 1: what its client (the Notosaurus app with a
licence, later the Android app) and the relay itself both import, so that they
can't drift apart.

The relay is notosaurus_core behind a licence key: each route is the remote form
of a core function (/v1/extract → llm.extract_cards…), takes what that function
takes but the AI configuration (the relay's own), and keeps nothing.

- Authentication: "Authorization: Bearer <licence key>".
- The client says its version in CLIENT_HEADER ("1.1.0"); a client too old for
  the relay gets "relay.client_outdated".
- The routes with photos (extract, revise, fix-card) take multipart/form-data: a "request"
  part holding the JSON request and one "images" part per photo (binary, as
  diagrams.prepare makes them: JPEG, at most 1568 px). The other routes take JSON.
- Errors: HTTP status of ERRORS, body {"code", "params"} (errors.AppError), the
  AI's own errors ("llm.*") passed on as they are.
- /v1/extract asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson" (STREAM_TYPE) answers as the
  AI writes: one JSON object per line, each card as it comes, then the answer or
  the error (ExtractLine). A client going away stops the AI.
- /v1/transcribe turns a dictation (the app's 🎤) into the text its speaker meant to
  type: multipart/form-data, a "request" part (TranscribeRequest) and an "audio" part
  (AUDIO_TYPES, at most MAX_AUDIO_BYTES).
- /v1/pictures/search finds free pictures of a subject to choose from (stock.search: public
  domain, CC0, Pixabay), their previews as data; /v1/pictures/found gives the one chosen,
  card size (JPEG), looked up again by its source and id. Both free: no AI, unless the
  search is asked `sort`ed (the AI keeps the pictures that show the subject: 1 credit);
  asked so with "Accept: application/x-ndjson", each source's pictures come as it
  answers (PictureSearchLine). Their pictures (and /v1/picture's) say where they come
  from in PICTURE_SOURCE_HEADER: kept with the card.
- /v1/revise asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson" says what the AI is at (slow, the
  fallback model), then the answer or the error (ReviseLine).
- /v1/fix-card: one card corrected by the user's request ("the answer is 1789"), seeing
  the lesson's photos: the AI writes that card alone (llm.fix_card).
- /v1/card-picture asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson" says each step as it begins
  (deciding, drawing, checking, redrawing with the first figure, searching), then the
  answer or the error (CardPictureLine).
- /v1/report: content the AI made, reported by the user (shocking, wrong…: Google Play's
  policy on generated content). The only thing the relay keeps of a lesson: what the user
  saw and sent, for REPORT_DAYS, read by Notosaurus. Free, REPORTS_PER_DAY a licence.
- /v1/speak reads a card's back aloud with one of /v1/voices (natural voices, the
  same on every device): an mp3, for the app that has no voices of its own.
- Each answer says the credits it used and those left (Usage; for /v1/picture and
  /v1/speak, the CREDITS_HEADER and CREDITS_LEFT_HEADER headers). A credit is a share of the
  call's real AI cost, at least 1 per call: the relay counts them, not the client.

The OpenAPI description (core/relay-api-v1.json) is generated from these models
by tools/relay_openapi.py. Apps already released keep calling the relay: within /v1 the
API only grows (new routes, optional request fields, answer fields more), checked against
the API each released app speaks (core/relay-api-releases/, tools/relay_compat.py).

post.description: Cards from the photos of a lesson (llm.extract_cards).

200.description: The cards; asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson": as the AI writes them, one ExtractLine per line.

images.description: The photos, in order: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, at most 4 MB each.

post.description: A natural-language correction of the cards (llm.revise_cards).

200.description: The cards corrected; asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson": what the AI is at, then the answer, one ReviseLine per line.

images.description: The photos, in order: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, at most 4 MB each.

post.description: One card corrected by the user's request (llm.fix_card).

images.description: The photos, in order: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, at most 4 MB each.

post.description: The lesson's own drawings for its cards, cut out of its photos (pictures.lesson_drawings).

images.description: The photos, in order: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, at most 4 MB each.

post.description: A card explained to the pupil (llm.explain_card).
A figure looked at against its description, what is wrong said (llm.check_figure).
A dictation as the text its speaker meant to type (llm.transcribe).

audio.description: The recording: audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/flac, at most 3 MB.

X-Notosaurus-Picture-Source.description: Where the picture comes from: a PictureSource, as JSON.

post.description: A card's figure or picture, the AI deciding which when needed (pictures.card_picture).

200.description: The card's picture; asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson": each step as it begins, then the answer, one CardPictureLine per line.

post.description: What a card's picture should be: a figure or a picture, described (llm.plan_picture).

Free pictures of a subject to choose from (stock.search). Free, unless `sort`ed by the AI
(stock.sorted_as_found): 1 credit.

200.description: The pictures found; `sort`ed and asked with "Accept: application/x-ndjson": each source's as it answers, one PictureSearchLine per line.

post.description: One of the pictures found (stock.fetch). Free.

X-Notosaurus-Picture-Source.description: Where the picture comes from: a PictureSource, as JSON.

post.description: A card's back read aloud with one of /v1/voices.
Content the AI made, reported by the user: kept REPORT_DAYS days, read by Notosaurus.

get.description: What the licence gives; also the connection test.

post.description: A Google Play subscription's licence: checked with Google Play; no key needed.
The free trial's licence (no card), once per phone: checked with Play Integrity; no key needed.

daily_left.title: Daily Left
daily_left.description: Credits that can still be used today.

ends_at.title: Ends At
ends_at.description: A subscription: when it ends unless renewed (ISO 8601); none for a licence without end.

on_hold.title: On Hold
on_hold.description: Past its end because a renewal's payment failed (Google Play's account hold): a payment to fix in Google Play, not a subscription ended.

notice.description: A message for every user, if any.

disabled.title: Disabled
disabled.description: FEATURES turned off for now: the app hides them and refuses them.

latest.title: Latest
latest.description: The latest version of the app ("1.2.0"); "" when not said.

drawing_credits.title: Drawing Credits
drawing_credits.description: About what a picture drawn by the image model costs, in credits (told to the user).

Account.title: Account
Account.description:
GET /v1/account: what the licence gives; also the client's connection test. And what
the app is told for now (set on the relay, no app update): a notice, the FEATURES
turned off, the latest version.

AiStep.description: What the AI is at, for the user waiting (calls.tell).

step.description: "slow": no answer yet after a while (the model busy); "fallback": the model not answering, the fallback one asked; "figures": the cards written, their figures being described.
step.title: Step

AiStep.title: AiStep

front.title: Front
front.description: Front: what is shown first (e.g. the word in the pupil's language), or the text with its gaps for a cloze card (see the rules).

back.title: Back
back.description: Back: the answer (e.g. the translation in the language being learned).

choices.title: Choices
choices.description: Only for a multiple-choice or true/false card (see the rules): the wrong options. Empty otherwise.

info.title: Info
info.description: Useful extra info: gender, plural, example… Empty if none.

subdeck.title: Subdeck
subdeck.description: Sub-deck (e.g. "Vocabulary", "Conjugation"). Empty for a single deck.

mask.description: Only for a diagram label (see the rules); otherwise null.

picture_prompt.title: Picture Prompt
picture_prompt.description: Only when the instructions ask for a picture on the card (see the rules): what to draw, in English. Empty otherwise.

picture_search.title: Picture Search
picture_search.description: Only with a picture_prompt, when the picture shows a real, specific thing that photos or paintings show (a person, a place, a monument, a work of art, an animal, an object, a food): a short search, in English, for a free picture of it ("Storming of the Bastille painting", "dog"). Empty when it must be drawn (an abstract word, an action, a scene made up for the card).

figure.title: Figure
figure.description: When an exact figure makes the card clearer (see the rules: geometry, or a notion the lesson's page shows a figure for): what to draw, every label with its exact text. Empty otherwise.

figure_kind.title: Figure Kind
figure_kind.description: With a figure, which kind it is: "geometry": points, segments, lines, circles, polygons, angles, their marks (a theorem, a construction); "graph": the graph of one or more functions in a frame; "sets": a Venn diagram of two or three sets; "diagram": boxes and arrows (a flowchart, a cycle, a chain, a classification); "circuit": an electric circuit; "chemistry": a molecule's formula written with its atoms' symbols and bonds (developed, semi-developed, skeletal, a ring), never a model of balls; "timeline": dates on a line; "other": anything else (a table, a labelled drawing, a solid in perspective, a map, a molecular model of coloured balls…). Empty otherwise.

fun_fact.title: Fun Fact
fun_fact.description: Only when fun facts are asked for (see the request): one short "did you know" sentence. Empty otherwise.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.description: Only when helps are asked for (see the request): why the answer is the answer, when understanding helps remember it. Empty otherwise.

mnemonic.title: Mnemonic
mnemonic.description: Only when helps are asked for (see the request): a natural way to remember the answer. Empty otherwise.

picture_on_back.title: Picture On Back
picture_on_back.description: True when the picture or figure belongs to the answer (see the rules); false when it is needed to answer.

doubt.description: Only when the lesson itself is clearly wrong on this card (see the rules); otherwise null.

CardPictureLine.description:
A line of /v1/card-picture asked as STREAM_TYPE, one of: {"step"} as each begins;
last, {"result"} or {"error"} (the HTTP status is 200 once a line is sent).
CardPictureLine.title: CardPictureLine

asked.title: Asked
asked.description: What the user wrote; null: none.

language.title: Language
language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").

fresh.title: Fresh
fresh.description: Draw it again rather than take it from the cache.

find.title: Find
find.description: A free picture looked for first, for a real thing.

draw.title: Draw
draw.description: A picture no free one fits drawn by the image model (it costs: the user said yes). False: 409 picture.needs_drawing instead, its params what was decided (description, search).

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: What /v1/check-figure found wrong in the card's figure: drawn again, told it (the user asked it). Empty: drawn as usual.

careful.title: Careful
careful.description: With a problem: drawn with the model's thinking (slower), not quickly.

CardPictureRequest.title: CardPictureRequest
CardPictureRequest.description:
A card's figure or picture (pictures.card_picture): its own, drawn as it is; or
what was written for it (any language), the AI deciding a figure or a picture. JSON.

card.description: The card, its picture's fields as decided (figure, picture_prompt…, picture_source).

data.title: Data
data.description: The figure's SVG or the picture's JPEG, base64.

CheckFigureRequest.title: CheckFigureRequest
CheckFigureRequest.description:
POST /v1/check-figure: a figure looked at against its description (the user asked it:
the "🔍 Check" button), as llm.check_figure. JSON.

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: What is wrong, in the cards' language; empty when it looks right.

deck.title: Deck
deck.description: Anki deck name, with :: for hierarchy (e.g. "Spanish::Lesson 5 - Family").

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One short sentence: what the lesson says, and what is right.

Doubt.title: Doubt
Doubt.description:
A card whose lesson is clearly wrong (a pupil's notes, a copy mistake): the card says
what the lesson says, this what is right; the parent chooses.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: Body of every error: a code the client translates, and its parameters.

language.title: Language
language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: The user's standing instructions, put before the request (never replacing the rules).

page_texts.title: Page Texts
page_texts.description: One per photo: the text of a PDF page, as the PDF holds it ("" for a photo).

ExplainRequest.title: ExplainRequest
ExplainRequest.description:
A card explained to the pupil (or an example, a way to remember it, why the
answer is right). JSON.

text.title: Text
text.description: The answer to the request, as asked: plain text, short.

more.title: More
more.description: The follow-ups that would truly help with this card, among "example", "mnemonic" and "why", not the one just given. Often one or none.

ExtractLine.description:
A line of /v1/extract's answer as the AI writes it (STREAM_TYPE), one of:
{"card"} as soon as a card is written; {"restart": true}: the cards sent so far
are dropped (another model starts again); {"step"}: what the AI is at; last,
{"result"} or {"error"} (the HTTP status is 200 once a line is sent: an error
comes as the last line). A client going away stops the AI: what it used is
charged, at least 1 credit.

card.description: A card as the AI wrote it (Card's fields, some missing).
card.title: Card

ExtractLine.title: ExtractLine

ExtractRequest.description: Cards from the photos (the "images" parts, in order), or from the prompt alone.

prompt.description: What to make of the lesson.
prompt.title: Prompt

decks.description: Decks that exist already, to reuse their names.
decks.title: Decks

pictures.description: Pictures where they truly help, even unasked by the prompt.
pictures.title: Pictures

page_texts.description: One per photo: the text of a PDF page, as the PDF holds it ("" for a photo).
page_texts.title: Page Texts

instructions.description: The user's standing instructions, put before the request (never replacing the rules).
instructions.title: Instructions

quick.description: Made fast: the AI thinks little (2 to 4 times faster, a little less careful).
quick.title: Quick

existing.description: The photos are a lesson's next pages: its cards made already ("front [part]"), not made again.
existing.title: Existing

ExtractRequest.title: ExtractRequest

description.title: Description
description.description: What to draw, every label exact.

FigureRequest.title: FigureRequest
FigureRequest.description: An exact figure (geometry, a labelled drawing), drawn as SVG. JSON.

svg.title: Svg
svg.description: The figure, cleaned: shapes and text only (figures.clean).

FixCardRequest.description:
One card corrected by a natural-language request, with the lesson's photos (the
"images" parts, possibly none).

prompt.description: What the cards were made with.
prompt.title: Prompt

language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").
language.title: Language

instructions.description: The user's standing instructions, put before the request (never replacing the rules).
instructions.title: Instructions

FixCardRequest.title: FixCardRequest

FoundPictureRequest.title: FoundPictureRequest
FoundPictureRequest.description:
POST /v1/pictures/found: one of the pictures found, as the card's. Answer: the JPEG
itself, card size.

page.title: Page
page.description: Number of the photo (1 = first photo).

box.title: Box
box.description: Box of the whole diagram (its drawing and all its labels), in the format of the instructions.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description: Where a diagram is on a photo: the image Anki gets is cropped to it.

card.title: Card
card.description: The card's index in the request.

data.title: Data
data.description: The drawing, cut out of its page: a JPEG, card size, base64.

LessonDrawingsRequest.description:
The drawings of their own the lesson's photos (the "images" parts) show for these
cards, cut out (pictures.lesson_drawings): the cards' pictures, before any is looked
for or drawn.
LessonDrawingsRequest.title: LessonDrawingsRequest

drawings.title: Drawings
drawings.description: Those found; the other cards none (look for theirs).

page.title: Page
page.description: Number of the photo showing the label (1 = first photo).

n.title: N
n.description: Number drawn in place of the label: 1, 2, 3… on each photo.

box.title: Box
box.description: Bounding box of the label's text, in the format of the instructions.

Mask.title: Mask

id.title: Id
id.description: Another id: shown again, even once closed.

texts.title: Texts
texts.description: By language ("fr", "en"…): the app shows its own, else English, else any.

Notice.title: Notice
Notice.description: A message for every user of the app, shown until closed (a problem being fixed…).

fresh.title: Fresh
fresh.description: Draw it again rather than reuse the last drawing.

search.title: Search
search.description: Card.picture_search: a free picture looked for first.

context.title: Context
context.description: The card, "front → back": to choose the picture found.

PictureRequest.title: PictureRequest
PictureRequest.description:
A picture for a card: a free one found when `search` is given and one fits (chosen
by the AI), else drawn by an image model. JSON; the answer is the JPEG itself.

PictureSearchLine.description:
A line of a sorted /v1/pictures/search asked as STREAM_TYPE, one of: {"found"},
the pictures a source gave that the AI kept, the best first, as each source answers;
last, {"done"} (its `results` empty: they came as "found") or {"error"} (the HTTP
status is 200 once a line is sent).
PictureSearchLine.title: PictureSearchLine

translate.title: Translate
translate.description: Written in any language: turned into English search words by the AI first.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: The AI keeps only the pictures that show the subject, the best first (it sees them): 1 credit, unless it couldn't sort them. Else free. Asked as STREAM_TYPE: PictureSearchLine.

PictureSearchRequest.title: PictureSearchRequest
PictureSearchRequest.description: Free pictures of a subject to choose from. JSON.

results.title: Results
results.description: The pictures found, at most 8, the sources taking turns.

words.title: Words
words.description: What was searched for (the translation, when asked).

usage.description: The credits charged: sorted by the AI only.

PictureSource.title: PictureSource
PictureSource.description:
Where a card's picture comes from, kept with the card (and, on the computer, in its
Anki note's hidden Source field): to check a free picture's page later, or find the
cards using one that must go.

PictureStep.description: What a card's picture is being made by, now (pictures.card_picture's steps).

step.description: "deciding": a figure or a picture; "drawing": a figure drawn, or a picture by the image model; "checking": the figure looked at; "redrawing": it was wrong, drawn again with the model's thinking; "searching": a free picture looked for.
step.title: Step

first.description: "redrawing": the first figure, its SVG (never kept).
first.title: First

PictureStep.title: PictureStep

asked.title: Asked
asked.description: What the user wrote, any language.

language.title: Language
language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").

PlanPictureRequest.title: PlanPictureRequest
PlanPictureRequest.description:
What a card's picture should be ("🎨 Draw"): an exact figure or an image model's
picture, described from the card and what the user wrote. JSON.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: "figure": something exact a clean drawing shows (geometry, a diagram, sets, a graph, a table, labels); "picture": a thing, an animal, a place, a person, a scene.

description.title: Description
description.description: A figure: what to draw, in the cards' language, every label with its exact text. A picture: what to draw, in English, one concrete subject a child recognises at once.

figure_kind.title: Figure Kind
figure_kind.description: A figure: which kind it is, "geometry": points, segments, lines, circles, polygons, angles, their marks (a theorem, a construction); "graph": the graph of one or more functions in a frame; "sets": a Venn diagram of two or three sets; "diagram": boxes and arrows (a flowchart, a cycle, a chain, a classification); "circuit": an electric circuit; "chemistry": a molecule's formula written with its atoms' symbols and bonds (developed, semi-developed, skeletal, a ring), never a model of balls; "timeline": dates on a line; "other": anything else (a table, a labelled drawing, a solid in perspective, a map, a molecular model of coloured balls…). Empty for a picture.

search.title: Search
search.description: A picture of a real, specific thing: a short English search for a free picture of it. Empty otherwise.

language.title: Language
language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").

RephraseRequest.title: RephraseRequest
RephraseRequest.description: A lesson's instructions tidied up: clear and short, every intention kept, none added. JSON.

content.title: Content
content.description: The content, as text: the card, its explanation, its picture's subject.

picture.title: Picture
picture.description: The card's picture, the AI's or a free one (never the user's photo): as a data URL; else empty.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: The instructions the lesson was made with.

language.title: Language
language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").

ReportRequest.title: ReportRequest
ReportRequest.description:
POST /v1/report: content the AI made, reported by the user. Only what they saw and
sent: never the lesson's photos, nor the child's name. JSON.

ReviseLine.description:
A line of /v1/revise asked as STREAM_TYPE, one of: {"step"}, what the AI is at;
last, {"result"} or {"error"} (the HTTP status is 200 once a line is sent).
ReviseLine.title: ReviseLine

ReviseRequest.description:
A natural-language correction of the cards, with the lesson's photos (the
"images" parts, possibly none).

prompt.description: What the cards were made with.
prompt.title: Prompt

language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").
language.title: Language

instructions.description: The user's standing instructions, put before the request (never replacing the rules).
instructions.title: Instructions

ReviseRequest.title: ReviseRequest

deck.title: Deck
deck.description: Anki deck name, with :: for hierarchy (e.g. "Spanish::Lesson 5 - Family").

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One short sentence describing what changed, in the requested language.

reverse.title: Reverse
reverse.description: "on" when the correction asks for the reverse card too (each card asked both ways), "off" when it asks for one way only; otherwise empty. Anki makes that card: never write it yourself.

typing.title: Typing
typing.description: "on" when the correction asks for the answers to be typed, "off" when it asks for them not to be; otherwise empty.

dictation.title: Dictation
dictation.description: "on" when the correction asks for a dictation of each card (hear the back, write it), "off" when it asks for none; otherwise empty. Anki makes that card: never write it yourself.

rate.title: Rate
rate.description: The speed: 1 normal, 0.9 a little slower.

SpeakRequest.title: SpeakRequest
SpeakRequest.description:
POST /v1/speak: a text read aloud. Answer: the mp3 (audio/mpeg), its credits in
CREDITS_HEADER and CREDITS_LEFT_HEADER (a share of the characters' real cost, at
least 1).

SubscribeRequest.title: SubscribeRequest
SubscribeRequest.description:
POST /v1/subscribe: a Google Play subscription bought (or restored, on another phone)
in the app; the relay checks it with Google Play and answers its licence key. The same
purchase always gives the same key: the phones of one subscription share its credits.

key.title: Key
key.description: The licence key, for the requests' Authorization header.

TranscribeRequest.description:
A dictation (the "audio" part) as the text its speaker meant to type: their words,
hesitations out, their own corrections applied, a lesson's foreign words spelled right.

kind.description: What it is for: a lesson's instructions, or a correction of its cards.
kind.title: Kind

language.description: English name of the language to answer in ("French").
language.title: Language

TranscribeRequest.title: TranscribeRequest

text.title: Text
text.description: What was said, as written text ("" when nothing was understood).

device.title: Device
device.description: The phone, as the app knows it (a SHA-256, in hex): the token's request hash is its own.

TrialRequest.title: TrialRequest
TrialRequest.description:
POST /v1/trial: the free trial, without a card: a few credits for a while, once per
phone. Play Integrity's token says it is the app from Google Play on a real phone; the
same phone always gets the same key (reinstalled: the trial's credits left, not new ones).

Voice.title: Voice
Voice.description: GET /v1/voices gives a list of them: the voices /v1/speak reads with.
